description: Small-displacement underbone motorcycle with a step-through frame, the most common vehicle on Thai roads.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Small underbone step-through motorcycle, low central footboard, plastic leg shield and tank cover, single seat with a pillion grab rail, spoked wheels, upright handlebars with mirrors, chain guard and rear luggage rack Materials: Glossy plastic body panels with decal stripes, chrome exhaust and mirror stems, dusty spoked rims, worn black seat vinyl, chain grease at the sprocket.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,976/4,000 triangles, 3/8 draw calls, 3/4 materials, 3/8 unique geometries, two 256 px canvases at 0.7 MB. Twenty-two tube runs open, eighteen thin chrome runs six-sided. Turntable: enclosed background is the step-through, the fork daylight and the gaps between the spokes, allowed on measurement.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at 0.712 x 1.258 x 1.895 m against a declared 0.71 x 1.25 x 1.92. Band table against the Meshy proxy (scratch/_mon/bands.mjs, ten bands, 5-95 pct, as a fraction of height): mean |dw| 0.021, mean |dd| 0.052 -- the second build measured 0.020 / 0.097 before the rack came down from 0.75 to the proxy's 0.545 H = 0.68 m (band 6 went from +0.448 to -0.065) and the fender lip and mudflap were lifted to hub height (band 1 +0.137 to +0.055). The one residual over 0.1 is band 2 at +0.125: the fender tip and the mudflap at hub height, which the plate shows and the proxy fuses away. Stations off the occupancy map: wheel centres 0.15 L / 0.80 L (z +0.64 / -0.58), bars at 1.00 m, mirror tips 1.258 m, seat top 0.76 m, leg shield 0.21-0.35 L.
featureReviews.notes: The first build read the map at a wrong length; the second put the rack 70 mm above the proxy's and was never measured against the band table -- it quoted stations only. This one quotes the table.

featureReviews.evidence: Front end: a 0.19 m navy FORK COVER on the fork line (z = 0.469 - 0.5095 (y - 0.6)) from the fender crown to the triple clamp -- the plate's widest front element, which the second build had as two 26 mm tubes -- with the chrome sliders through the hub below it, a lower yoke, stem, pulled-back bars with black grips, mirror stems to 0.124 m heads, a 0.146 m headlamp with a proud lens in a cowl whose top edges are filleted at 45 mm, two amber pods, an instrument. Mid: a navy frame SPINE floors the step-through from the shield's back (y 0.31-0.45 at z +0.46) to the seat nose (0.69 at z +0.14), with the engine under it -- crankcase, a 0.19 m clutch cover, and the barrel and finned head laid 74 degrees forward as a Cub's is (the second build canted it 20 degrees, a vertical single). Chain runs to a rear sprocket under the guard, dull #7a766f exhaust on the right, painted swingarm, shocks, pegs, kickstart, stand. Tail: chrome rack at 0.70 m with its raised rail, four struts and three slats, tail lamp on its bracket, amber indicators on stalks, mudflap to hub height.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's leg shield reads as a wrapped apron and the second build's was a slab: its outer front edges now wrap back on an 85 mm plan radius, and the seat carries 45 mm shoulders with 60 mm end roundings.

featureReviews.evidence: Two instanced OPEN wire wheels at one geometry: a closed tyre-ring lathe (16 segments), a rim ring, a 0.164 m drum hub with a chrome cap and twenty-six three-sided prism spokes (eighteen before; the plate's wheel reads as a dense wire fan), with real daylight between them. Tread UVs around-by-profile at 0.05 m per repeat; rim, hub and spokes pin to the tile's white top 4%. Pivots wheel-front and wheel-rear on the axles.
featureReviews.notes: 648 triangles per geometry, drawn twice through one InstancedMesh.

featureReviews.evidence: Plate and hero render measured at the same regions with PIL. The second build's navy #343f58 rendered the lit shield flank at (78,86,104), luma 86 sat 0.25, against the plate's (60,71,101), luma 71 sat 0.40: the harness renders a lit side face at R = 0.72 A + 40, so the paint is authored at #22305a and now measures (59,69,97), luma 69 sat 0.39. Seat crown 84 against the plate's 91 (was 67); engine cases 138 against 135; chrome 143-163 against the plate's 128-164 (rack was 210 at #b9bcbf, now #a0a2a4); rear fender 43 sat 0.37 against 50 sat 0.21. The tyre renders 87 against a measured 74, lifted on purpose for the back-lit frame. Roughness 0.34 on the paint for the plate's hard highlights. Two post-construction canvases: dust on the paint, tread on the rubber.
featureReviews.notes: Chrome without metalness because the harness has no environment map; the chrome therefore reads flat rather than mirrored, which is the material layer's remaining gap.

notes: Budget class overridden from medium to large. At 1.92 m longest dimension the size rule says medium, which allows 2 draw calls and 2 materials -- not enough for a motorcycle, which needs the frame and wheels as bare metal separate from the painted plastic bodywork and the black seat and tyres. The bike is small but not simple, and the medium ceiling would force the wheels into the same material as the body. No destruction groups: it is a parking and traffic prop, not a breakable. Declared height corrected 1.07 -> 1.25 on 2026-08-28: the list-time 1.07 was to the bar tops, and the Meshy proxy (scratch/honda-wave/_ev, bbox 1.897 x 1.240 x 0.727) normalises to L:H:W 1 : 0.654 : 0.383, so at the declared 1.92 m length the mirror tips stand at 1.240/1.897 x 1.92 = 1.255 m and the width is 0.383 x 1.92 = 0.735. Built envelope 0.712 x 1.258 x 1.891.
